as_told.title: PEER project trains abductees to question their abductors

plain: Around 2004 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, a lawyer named Dan Sheehan and a Harvard figure named John Mack decided to train people who had "consistent repeated encounters" with beings they said abducted them, using holotropic breathing, a deep breathing method meant to bring on altered states. Sheehan tells Michels he took part and was legal counsel for Mack's group, PEER, the Project for Extraordinary Experience Research. In another conversation he tells it differently: he names PEER, says the aim was to teach abductees to question their abductors, and does not mention the breathing.
